```{python}
#| output: false
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../theme")
import bse_style, bse_anim
_ = bse_style.apply()

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy import stats
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf

T_COL, C_COL = bse_style.ORANGE, bse_style.TEAL   # treated = orange, control = teal
PURPLE, GRAY = bse_style.PURPLE, "#9A9A9A"

def md_table(rows, header, align=None):
    align = align or ["l"] + ["r"] * (len(header) - 1)
    sep = {"l": ":---", "r": "---:", "c": ":---:"}
    out = ["| " + " | ".join(header) + " |", "|" + "|".join(sep[a] for a in align) + "|"]
    out += ["| " + " | ".join(r) + " |" for r in rows]
    print("\n" + "\n".join(out) + "\n")

def stars(p):
    return "***" if p < 0.01 else "**" if p < 0.05 else "*" if p < 0.10 else ""

def reg(formula, data):
    return smf.ols(formula, data).fit(cov_type="HC1")      # robust (HC1) standard errors

FENCE = "`" * 3   # a literal fence at line start would end a Quarto cell

def sm_summary(fit, font=0.55):
    """Full statsmodels summary(), rendered as an academic (booktabs-style) table."""
    xn = [v.replace("C(city)[T.", "city[").replace("treat:", "treat × ") for v in fit.params.index]
    sm = fit.summary(xname=xn)
    html = "".join(t.as_html() for t in sm.tables)
    notes = "<br>".join(sm.extra_txt.splitlines()) if sm.extra_txt else ""
    print(f"\n{FENCE}{{=html}}\n<div class='sm-summary' style='font-size:{font}em'>{html}"
          f"<div class='sm-notes'>{notes}</div></div>\n{FENCE}\n")

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Simulated RCT in a ride-hailing app (the same code is in TA6.ipynb)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CITIES = ["Madrid", "Barcelona", "Paris", "London"]

def simulate_app(n=4000, seed=669):
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    # pre-treatment covariates
    city = rng.choice(CITIES, n, p=[0.3, 0.3, 0.2, 0.2])
    age = np.clip(rng.normal(34, 9, n).round(), 18, 70).astype(int)
    tenure = np.clip(rng.exponential(20, n).round(), 1, 96).astype(int)           # months on the app
    base = pd.Series(city).map({"Madrid": 3.0, "Barcelona": 3.5, "Paris": 4.5, "London": 5.5}).values
    fare = pd.Series(city).map({"Madrid": 11, "Barcelona": 12, "Paris": 16, "London": 19}).values \
        * rng.lognormal(0, 0.15, n)                                                 # user's usual fare (€)
    mu_pre = base * np.exp(-0.02 * (age - 34)) * (0.7 + 0.6 * np.minimum(tenure, 48) / 48)
    rides_pre = rng.poisson(mu_pre * rng.gamma(1.5, 1 / 1.5, n))                   # rides in the 4 weeks before
    revenue_pre = np.round(rides_pre * fare * rng.uniform(0.9, 1.1, n), 2)         # € spent in the 4 weeks before
    # random assignment
    treat = rng.binomial(1, 0.5, n)
    # would the user pick "Wait & Save" if offered? (heavy and young users more likely)
    p_choose = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(-0.4 + 0.15 * (rides_pre - 4) - 0.04 * (age - 34))))
    would_choose = rng.binomial(1, p_choose)
    # potential outcomes in the 4 weeks of the test
    tau = np.clip(pd.Series(city).map({"Madrid": 0.3, "Barcelona": 0.8, "Paris": 1.8, "London": 3.0}).values
                  + 0.03 * (34 - age), 0, None)                                    # extra rides from the new option
    rides0 = rng.poisson(0.8 * rides_pre + 0.02 * tenure + 0.5)                    # rides with app A
    new_rides = rng.poisson(tau) * would_choose                                    # NEW rides, at 75% of the fare
    switched = rng.binomial(rides0, 0.5) * would_choose                            # usual rides switched to W&S (-25%)
    rev0 = rides0 * fare                                                           # revenue with app A
    rev1 = rev0 - 0.25 * fare * switched + 0.75 * fare * new_rides                 # revenue with app B
    # what we observe
    rides_post = np.where(treat == 1, rides0 + new_rides, rides0)
    revenue_post = np.round(np.where(treat == 1, rev1, rev0), 2)
    df = pd.DataFrame(dict(user_id=np.arange(1, n + 1), city=city, age=age, tenure=tenure,
                           rides_pre=rides_pre, revenue_pre=revenue_pre, treat=treat,
                           chose_wait_save=treat * would_choose, rides_post=rides_post,
                           revenue_post=revenue_post))
    return df, pd.DataFrame(dict(rev0=rev0, rev1=rev1))

app, truth = simulate_app()
app["city"] = pd.Categorical(app.city, categories=CITIES)   # Madrid = base category
true_ate = (truth.rev1 - truth.rev0).mean()
```

# 1 · Potential outcomes {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

---

## Potential outcomes

$$
\begin{array}{rcl}
D_i \in \{0,1\} & \qquad & \text{treatment indicator} \\[2pt]
Y_i(1) & & \text{potential outcome } \textbf{with} \text{ treatment} \\[2pt]
Y_i(0) & & \text{potential outcome } \textbf{without} \text{ treatment} \\[2pt]
\tau_i = Y_i(1) - Y_i(0) & & \text{individual causal effect}
\end{array}
$$

::: {.fragment}
What we observe:

::: {.eq-box-wrap style="margin:0.2em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$Y_i \;=\; D_i\,Y_i(1) + (1-D_i)\,Y_i(0) \;=\; \begin{cases} Y_i(1) & \text{if } D_i = 1 \\ Y_i(0) & \text{if } D_i = 0 \end{cases}$$
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment}
::: {.callout-warning title="The fundamental problem of causal inference" icon=false}
We **never** observe both $Y_i(1)$ and $Y_i(0)$ for the same person: causality is a **missing data** problem.
:::
:::

---

## Example: does smoking during pregnancy reduce birthweight?

```{python}
#| output: asis
np.random.seed(42)
n = 200
mother_age = np.random.normal(27, 5, n).clip(17, 40)
p_smoke = 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(35 - mother_age) / 2))     # younger mothers smoke more
smoke = np.random.binomial(1, p_smoke)
Y0 = 3000 + 40 * (mother_age - 25) + np.random.normal(0, 150, n)
Y1 = 2800 + 20 * (mother_age - 25) + np.random.normal(0, 150, n)
bw = np.where(smoke == 1, Y1, Y0)
sim = pd.DataFrame(dict(age=mother_age, smoke=smoke, Y0=Y0, Y1=Y1, bw=bw))
sim = pd.concat([sim[sim.smoke == 1].sample(20, random_state=1),
                 sim[sim.smoke == 0].sample(10, random_state=1)])
sim["cf"] = np.where(sim.smoke == 1, sim.Y0, sim.Y1)
sm_, ns_ = sim[sim.smoke == 1], sim[sim.smoke == 0]

s = bse_anim.Steps("bw", figsize=(9.6, 4.6), margins=dict(left=0.09, right=0.74))
ax = s.ax
ax.set_xlim(16, 41); ax.set_ylim(2350, 3600)
ax.set_xlabel("Mother's age"); ax.set_ylabel("Birthweight (g)")
ax.scatter(ns_.age, ns_.bw, s=70, color=C_COL, edgecolor="black", lw=0.6, zorder=3, label="Non-smoker")
ax.scatter(sm_.age, sm_.bw, s=70, color=T_COL, edgecolor="black", lw=0.6, zorder=3, label="Smoker")
ax.set_title("What we observe")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), fontsize=11)
s.snap()
ax.scatter(sm_.age, sm_.cf, s=70, facecolor="none", edgecolor=T_COL, lw=1.6, zorder=3, label="Smoker, if not smoking")
ax.scatter(ns_.age, ns_.cf, s=70, facecolor="none", edgecolor=C_COL, lw=1.6, zorder=3, label="Non-smoker, if smoking")
ax.set_title("What we would need: the counterfactuals (hollow)")
ax.legend(loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1), fontsize=11)
s.snap()
for _, r in sim.iterrows():
    ax.plot([r.age, r.age], [r.bw, r.cf], color=T_COL if r.smoke else C_COL, alpha=0.45, lw=1.3, zorder=2)
ax.set_title(r"Individual effects $\tau_i = Y_i(1) - Y_i(0)$ — never observed")
s.snap()
s.show(height=480)
```

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.75em; text-align:center;"}
Each vertical segment is one $\tau_i$. We only ever see **one end** of it.
:::

---

## Two averages of $\tau_i$: ATE and ATT

::: {.eq-box-wrap}
::: {.eq-box}
$$\text{ATE} = E[Y(1) - Y(0)] \qquad\qquad \text{ATT} = E[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid D = 1]$$
:::
:::

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.9em"}
- **ATE**: average effect over **everyone**. *"What if all mothers smoked vs. none?"*
- **ATT**: average effect over the **treated** only. *"How much lighter are smokers' babies because their mothers smoked?"*
:::

::: {.fragment}
What does the naive comparison of means estimate?

::: {.eq-box-wrap style="font-size:0.85em; margin:0.2em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$\underbrace{E[Y \mid D = 1] - E[Y \mid D = 0]}_{\text{naive comparison}} \;=\; \underbrace{E[Y(1) - Y(0) \mid D = 1]}_{\text{ATT}} \;+\; \underbrace{E[Y(0) \mid D = 1] - E[Y(0) \mid D = 0]}_{\text{selection bias}}$$
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.8em; text-align:center"}
**Age is a confounder:** younger mothers smoke more **and** have lighter babies anyway ⇒ selection bias ≠ 0, so the naive comparison is neither the ATT nor the ATE.
:::
:::

# 2 · Randomization {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

---

## Randomization kills selection bias

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
If $D_i$ is assigned by a **coin flip**, it cannot depend on anything about the mother, observed or not:
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
np.random.seed(7)
Nn = 4000
age_ = np.random.normal(27, 5, Nn).clip(17, 40)
d_self = np.random.binomial(1, 1 / (1 + np.exp(-(30 - age_) / 2.5)))
d_rand = np.random.binomial(1, 0.5, Nn)
bins = np.arange(17, 41, 1)
s = bse_anim.Steps("random", figsize=(10, 3.9), ncols=2, sharey=True,
                   margins=dict(left=0.07, right=0.98, bottom=0.16, top=0.86, wspace=0.08))
a1, a2 = s.ax
for a, d, ttl in [(a1, d_self, "Self-selection: mothers choose"), (a2, d_rand, "Randomization: coin flip")]:
    a.hist(age_[d == 0], bins=bins, density=True, color=C_COL, alpha=0.6, label="D = 0")
    a.hist(age_[d == 1], bins=bins, density=True, color=T_COL, alpha=0.6, label="D = 1")
    a.axvline(age_[d == 0].mean(), color=C_COL, lw=2.5); a.axvline(age_[d == 1].mean(), color=T_COL, lw=2.5)
    a.set_title(ttl); a.set_xlabel("Mother's age")
a1.set_ylabel("Density"); a1.legend(loc="upper right")
a2.set_visible(False); s.snap()
a2.set_visible(True); s.snap()
s.show(height=255)
```

::: {.fragment}
::: {.eq-box-wrap style="font-size:0.8em; margin:0.1em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$\begin{aligned}
\big(Y(1), Y(0)\big) \perp\!\!\!\perp D \;&\Longrightarrow\; \underbrace{E[Y(0) \mid D = 1] - E[Y(0) \mid D = 0]}_{\text{selection bias} \;=\; 0} \\[2pt]
&\Longrightarrow\; E[Y \mid D = 1] - E[Y \mid D = 0] \;=\; \text{ATT} \;=\; \text{ATE}
\end{aligned}$$
:::
:::
:::

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.72em"}
::: {.callout-warning title="Caveat" icon=false}
Here randomization is **not an option**: assigning pregnant women to smoke would be **unethical** (and infeasible). For questions like this we need **observational** methods: matching, IV, RDD, DiD (the next TAs).
:::
:::

# 3 · An RCT in a ride-hailing app {background-color="#0396A6" .section-divider-centered}

---

## The case: a new, cheaper option in the app

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
*Ryde*, a (fictional) ride-hailing app, wants to add **one** new option to the menu:
**"Wait & Save"**: ~25% cheaper if you accept being picked up in 10–15 minutes.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
CAR = ('<svg viewBox="0 0 38 20"><path d="M4 13 L6 8 Q7 6 9 6 L27 6 Q29 6 31 8 L34 12 Q36 12.5 36 14 L36 15 '
       'L2 15 L2 14 Q2 13 4 13 Z" fill="{c}"/><path d="M10 7.5 L26 7.5 L29 11 L8 11 Z" fill="#cfe0ea"/>'
       '<circle cx="10" cy="15.5" r="2.8" fill="#222"/><circle cx="28" cy="15.5" r="2.8" fill="#222"/></svg>')
MAP = """<svg viewBox="0 0 220 300" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid slice">
<rect width="220" height="300" fill="#E9EBEE"/>
<path d="M-10 230 C 60 200, 120 260, 230 215 L230 250 C 130 290, 60 235, -10 265 Z" fill="#CFE2F3"/>
<rect x="128" y="72" width="62" height="48" rx="4" fill="#D5EBD7"/>
<g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="7" fill="none">
<path d="M-10 60 L230 85"/><path d="M-10 150 L230 160"/><path d="M40 -10 L60 310"/>
<path d="M115 -10 L105 310"/><path d="M180 -10 L200 310"/><path d="M-10 0 L230 210"/></g>
<g stroke="#FFFFFF" stroke-width="3" fill="none">
<path d="M-10 110 L230 120"/><path d="M-10 195 L230 190"/><path d="M80 -10 L80 310"/><path d="M150 -10 L150 310"/></g>
<path d="M58 168 L80 166 L80 118 L150 120 L150 82" stroke="#000" stroke-width="3.5" fill="none" stroke-linejoin="round"/>
<circle cx="58" cy="168" r="6" fill="#000"/><circle cx="58" cy="168" r="2.4" fill="#fff"/>
<rect x="144" y="76" width="12" height="12" fill="#000"/><rect x="148" y="80" width="4" height="4" fill="#fff"/>
</svg>"""
STATUS = ('<div class="status"><span>9:41</span><span><svg width="44" height="11" viewBox="0 0 44 11">'
          '<rect x="0" y="7" width="3" height="4" rx="1"/><rect x="4.5" y="5" width="3" height="6" rx="1"/>'
          '<rect x="9" y="2.5" width="3" height="8.5" rx="1"/><rect x="13.5" y="0" width="3" height="11" rx="1"/>'
          '<rect x="22" y="0.5" width="19" height="10" rx="3" fill="none" stroke="#000" stroke-width="1"/>'
          '<rect x="24" y="2.5" width="13" height="6" rx="1.5"/><rect x="42" y="3.5" width="1.6" height="4" rx="0.8"/>'
          '</svg></span></div>')

def phone(new=False):
    opts = [("Economy", "4 min · 4 seats", "€12.40", "#3b3b3b", "selected"),
            ("Comfort", "5 min · newer cars", "€15.90", "#5f6b75", ""),
            ("XL", "7 min · 6 seats", "€21.10", "#1f2a33", "")]
    if new:
        opts.append(('Wait &amp; Save<span class="badge">NEW</span>', "Pick-up in 10–15 min", "€9.30", "#F28627", "new"))
    rows = "".join(f'<div class="opt {cls}">{CAR.format(c=col)}<div class="txt"><b>{name}</b><span>{sub}</span></div>'
                   f'<div class="price">{price}</div></div>' for name, sub, price, col, cls in opts)
    return (f'<div class="iphone"><div class="screen"><div class="island"></div>{STATUS}'
            f'<div class="map">{MAP}<div class="where"><div><i class="dot"></i>Plaça de Catalunya</div>'
            f'<div><i></i>Sagrada Família</div></div></div>'
            f'<div class="sheet"><div class="handle"></div><div class="sheet-title">Choose a ride</div>{rows}'
            f'<div class="pay">💳 Visa •••• 4242</div><div class="request">Request ride</div></div>'
            f'<div class="homebar"></div></div></div>')

print(f"""
{FENCE}{{=html}}
<div class="phones">
  <div class="phone-col"><div class="phone-label" style="color:{C_COL}">A · Control (D = 0)</div>{phone()}</div>
  <div class="phone-col fragment"><div class="phone-label" style="color:{T_COL}">B · Treatment (D = 1)</div>{phone(new=True)}</div>
</div>
{FENCE}
""")
```

::: {.fragment .hyp-box}
**Hypothesis:** **IF** we add an option **"Wait & Save"** **THEN** price-sensitive users who today take the bus or walk will now request a ride bringing more **revenue**.
:::

---

## Designing the experiment

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
- **Outcome** $Y_i$: **revenue** from user $i$ in the 4 weeks of the test.
- **Treatment** $D_i = 1$ if user $i$ sees app **B** (with "Wait & Save"), $D_i = 0$ if app **A** (current menu).
- **Units:** active users, each randomly assigned to A or B with probability ½ (a coin flip per user).
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
rng_ = np.random.default_rng(11)
NR, NC = 5, 10
d_demo = rng_.permutation(np.r_[np.ones(25, int), np.zeros(25, int)])
s = bse_anim.Steps("assign", figsize=(11.5, 3.8), margins=dict(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.99, bottom=0.01))
ax = s.ax
ax.set_xlim(0, 23.2); ax.set_ylim(-0.9, 6.6); ax.axis("off"); ax.set_aspect("equal")
sq = 0.78
def grid(x0, y0, colors, ncol):
    for k, col in enumerate(colors):
        ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((x0 + (k % ncol) * 1.0, y0 - (k // ncol) * 1.0), sq, sq, color=col, lw=0))
grid(0.2, 4.6, ["#BDBDBD"] * 50, NC)
ax.text(5.1, 5.75, f"{len(app):,} active users", ha="center", fontsize=14, fontweight="bold")
ax.text(5.1, -0.75, "pre-treatment info: city, age, tenure, past rides and spending", ha="center", fontsize=11, color="#666")
s.snap()
grid(0.2, 4.6, [T_COL if d else C_COL for d in d_demo], NC)
ax.annotate("", xy=(13.4, 2.9), xytext=(10.6, 2.9), arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="-|>", color=PURPLE, lw=2.5, mutation_scale=20))
ax.text(12.0, 3.35, "coin flip", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=PURPLE)
s.snap()
grid(14.0, 4.6, [T_COL] * 25, 9); grid(14.0, 1.0, [C_COL] * 25, 9)
ax.text(18.4, 5.75, f"B · treatment (n = {app.treat.sum():,})", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=T_COL, fontweight="bold")
ax.text(18.4, 2.15, f"A · control (n = {(1 - app.treat).sum():,})", ha="center", fontsize=13, color=C_COL, fontweight="bold")
s.snap()
s.show(height=320)
```

## The data

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
We simulate the experiment (code in the notebook) for 4,000 users. Relevant variables:

- `revenue_post`: $Y_i$, revenue (€) from user $i$ during the 4 weeks of the test
- `treat`: $D_i$, equal to 1 if app **B** (with "Wait & Save"), 0 if app **A**
- `city`, `age`, `tenure` (months on the app), `rides_pre`, `revenue_pre` (rides and € in the 4 weeks **before**): pre-treatment covariates $X_i$
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.95em; margin-top:0.6em"}
```{python}
#| echo: true
app[["user_id", "city", "age", "tenure", "rides_pre", "revenue_pre", "treat", "revenue_post"]].head()
```
:::

---

## ATE = difference in means

Randomization ⇒ no selection bias ⇒ $\;\text{ATE} = E[Y \mid D = 1] - E[Y \mid D = 0]$, estimated by $\;\widehat{\text{ATE}} = \bar Y_1 - \bar Y_0$.

::: {.eq-box-wrap style="font-size:0.85em; margin:0.2em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$\begin{gathered}
H_0:\ E[Y \mid D = 1] = E[Y \mid D = 0] \qquad\quad H_a:\ E[Y \mid D = 1] \neq E[Y \mid D = 0] \\[6pt]
t = \frac{\bar Y_1 - \bar Y_0}{\sqrt{s_1^2/n_1 + s_0^2/n_0}} \;\overset{H_0}{\approx}\; N(0,1)
\end{gathered}$$
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
Welch two-sample $t$-test (unequal variances): reject $H_0$ at 5% if $|t| > 1.96$.
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
```{python}
#| echo: true
y1 = app.loc[app.treat == 1, "revenue_post"]          # D = 1 (app B)
y0 = app.loc[app.treat == 0, "revenue_post"]          # D = 0 (app A)
print(f"mean(D=1) = {y1.mean():.2f}   mean(D=0) = {y0.mean():.2f}   difference = {y1.mean() - y0.mean():.2f}")
res = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)          # Welch t-test
print(f"t = {res.statistic:.3f}   p-value = {res.pvalue:.4f}   df = {res.df:.1f}")
```
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
tt = stats.ttest_ind(y1, y0, equal_var=False)
decision = ("we **reject** $H_0$ at 5%" if tt.pvalue < 0.05
            else "we **cannot reject** $H_0$ at 5%: the estimate is positive, but too noisy")
print(f"""
::: {{.fragment style="font-size:0.85em"}}
$t = {tt.statistic:.2f}$, $\;p = {tt.pvalue:.3f}$ ⇒ {decision}.
:::
""")
```

---

## … which is the same as a regression on $D$

$$\texttt{revenue}\_\texttt{post}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 D_i + \varepsilon_i$$

```{python}
#| output: asis
r1 = reg("revenue_post ~ treat", app)
sm_summary(r1, font=0.52)
```

---

## Are treatment and control truly random?

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
If randomization worked, B and A look alike **before** the test. For each pre-treatment covariate $X_k$:
:::

::: {.eq-box-wrap style="font-size:0.8em; margin:0.2em 0"}
::: {.eq-box}
$$H_0:\ E[X_k \mid D = 1] = E[X_k \mid D = 0] \qquad t_k = \frac{\bar X_{k,1} - \bar X_{k,0}}{\sqrt{s_{k,1}^2/n_1 + s_{k,0}^2/n_0}}$$
:::
:::

::: {style="font-size:0.56em"}
```{python}
#| output: asis
for c in CITIES:
    app[c] = (app.city == c).astype(int)
BAL = [("age", "Age"), ("tenure", "Tenure (months)"), ("rides_pre", "Rides before"),
       ("revenue_pre", "Revenue before (€)")] + [(c, f"City = {c} (share)") for c in CITIES]
rows = []
for v, lab in BAL:
    a, b = app[v][app.treat == 1], app[v][app.treat == 0]
    t_ = stats.ttest_ind(a, b, equal_var=False)
    rows.append([lab, f"{a.mean():.3f}", f"{b.mean():.3f}", f"{a.mean() - b.mean():+.3f}", f"{t_.statistic:.2f}", f"{t_.pvalue:.2f}"])
md_table(rows, ["$X_k$", "$\\bar X_{k,1}$", "$\\bar X_{k,0}$", "Diff.", "$t_k$", "p"])
ja = smf.ols("treat ~ age + tenure + rides_pre + revenue_pre + C(city)", app).fit()
```
:::

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.7em"}
```{python}
#| output: asis
print(f"No difference is significant ✅ (with many tests, ~1 in 20 rejects at 5% by chance). Joint check, regressing $D$ on all $X$: $F$ = {ja.fvalue:.2f}, $p$ = {ja.f_pvalue:.2f}.")
```
:::

---

## Using covariates to estimate the ATE

$$\texttt{revenue}\_\texttt{post}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 D_i + \gamma_1\,\texttt{age}_i + \gamma_2\,\texttt{tenure}_i + \gamma_3\,\texttt{revenue}\_\texttt{pre}_i + \textstyle\sum_c \delta_c\,\text{city}_{c,i} + \varepsilon_i$$

```{python}
#| output: asis
r3 = reg("revenue_post ~ treat + C(city) + age + tenure + revenue_pre", app)
sm_summary(r3, font=0.44)
```

---

## Covariates shrink the CI, not the bias

```{python}
#| output: asis
specs = [("revenue_post ~ treat", "(1) No controls"),
         ("revenue_post ~ treat + C(city) + age + tenure", "(2) + city, age, tenure"),
         ("revenue_post ~ treat + C(city) + age + tenure + revenue_pre", "(3) + revenue before")]
fits = [(lab, reg(f, app)) for f, lab in specs]
lo = min(f.params.treat - 1.96 * f.bse.treat for _, f in fits); hi = max(f.params.treat + 1.96 * f.bse.treat for _, f in fits)
s = bse_anim.Steps("coefplot", figsize=(9.5, 3.3), margins=dict(left=0.29, right=0.97, top=0.86, bottom=0.21))
ax = s.ax
ax.set_xlim(min(lo, 0) - 0.5, hi + 0.35 * (hi - min(lo, 0))); ax.set_ylim(-0.6, 2.6); ax.invert_yaxis()
ax.set_yticks(range(3)); ax.set_yticklabels([lab for lab, _ in fits], fontsize=13)
ax.axvline(0, color="black", lw=1); ax.set_xlabel(r"$\hat\beta_1$ with 95% CI (€ per user, 4 weeks)")
for k, (lab, f) in enumerate(fits):
    b, se = f.params.treat, f.bse.treat
    col = [GRAY, PURPLE, T_COL][k]
    ax.plot([b - 1.96 * se, b + 1.96 * se], [k, k], color=col, lw=5, solid_capstyle="round", alpha=0.8)
    ax.scatter([b], [k], s=120, color=col, edgecolor="black", zorder=3)
    ax.text(b + 1.96 * se + 0.2, k, f"{b:.2f}  (se {se:.2f})", va="center", fontsize=13, color=col)
    ax.set_title("Same estimate, narrower interval"); s.snap()
s.show(height=310)
md_table([["$R^2$"] + [f"{f.rsquared:.3f}" for _, f in fits],
          ["$p$-value of $\\hat\\beta_1$"] + [f"{f.pvalues.treat:.3f}" for _, f in fits]],
         [""] + [lab for lab, _ in fits], align=["l", "c", "c", "c"])
```

::: {.fragment style="font-size:0.8em"}
- **Estimate barely moves:** $X \perp\!\!\!\perp D$ by design, so controlling for $X$ removes no bias (there is none), only chance imbalance.
- **SE shrinks:** past spending predicts future spending very well → less residual variance → **more precision / power**.
- Only **pre-treatment** covariates (never something the treatment could change).
:::

---

## Heterogeneous treatment effects: by city

$$\texttt{revenue}\_\texttt{post}_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 D_i + \textstyle\sum_{c \neq \text{Madrid}} \delta_c\,\text{city}_{c,i} + \sum_{c \neq \text{Madrid}} \theta_c\,(D_i \times \text{city}_{c,i}) + \varepsilon_i$$

```{python}
#| output: asis
hc = reg("revenue_post ~ treat * C(city)", app)
sm_summary(hc, font=0.42)
```

---

## Heterogeneous treatment effects: by city

```{python}
#| output: asis
names = list(hc.params.index)
city_eff = []
for c in CITIES:
    L = np.zeros(len(names)); L[names.index("treat")] = 1
    if c != CITIES[0]:
        L[names.index(f"treat:C(city)[T.{c}]")] = 1
    tt_ = hc.t_test(L); city_eff.append((c, float(tt_.effect[0]), float(np.squeeze(tt_.sd))))
ftest = hc.f_test(", ".join(f"treat:C(city)[T.{c}] = 0" for c in CITIES[1:]))
ate_hat = r1.params.treat
s = bse_anim.Steps("hte", figsize=(9, 3.9), margins=dict(left=0.11, right=0.97, top=0.88, bottom=0.12))
ax = s.ax
ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=1)
ax.set_xticks(range(len(CITIES))); ax.set_xticklabels(CITIES); ax.set_xlim(-0.6, len(CITIES) - 0.4)
lo = min(b - 1.96 * se for _, b, se in city_eff); hi = max(b + 1.96 * se for _, b, se in city_eff)
ax.set_ylim(min(lo, 0) - 1, hi + 1.5); ax.set_ylabel(r"Effect of B on revenue, $\beta_1 + \theta_c$ (€)")
ax.axhline(ate_hat, color=PURPLE, ls="--", lw=1.8)
ax.text(-0.55, ate_hat + 0.4, f"ATE = {ate_hat:.2f}", color=PURPLE, fontsize=12)
ax.set_title("Overall ATE")
s.snap()
for k, (lab, b, se) in enumerate(city_eff):
    ax.errorbar(k, b, yerr=1.96 * se, fmt="o", ms=11, color=T_COL, mec="black", capsize=7, lw=2.5)
    ax.text(k + 0.1, b, f"{b:.2f}", va="center", fontsize=12)
ax.set_title("Effect by city (95% CI)")
s.snap()
s.show(height=380)
ranked = sorted(city_eff, key=lambda e: -e[1])
fp = float(ftest.pvalue)
verdict = ("we **reject** that the effect is the same in every city" if fp < 0.05
           else "we **cannot reject** that the effect is the same in every city")
neg = [c for c, b, _ in city_eff if b < 0]
neg_txt = (f" In **{' and '.join(neg)}** the estimate is **negative**: users mostly switch to the cheaper option instead of riding more, so revenue falls."
           if neg else "")
print(f"""
::: {{.fragment style="font-size:0.8em"}}
Joint test $H_0: \\theta_{{BCN}} = \\theta_{{PAR}} = \\theta_{{LON}} = 0$: $F$ = {float(np.squeeze(ftest.fvalue)):.2f}, $p$ = {fp:.3f} → {verdict}.
Revenue rises most in **{ranked[0][0]}** (€{ranked[0][1]:.2f}) and **{ranked[1][0]}** (€{ranked[1][1]:.2f}).{neg_txt}
Randomization holds within each city, so each city effect is causal (but pre-specify subgroups: slice the data 20 ways and one will look significant by chance).
:::
""")
```

## Take-up: offering ≠ using

::: {style="font-size:0.85em"}
We can **offer** "Wait & Save" (app B), but we cannot force users to **choose** it.

```{python}
#| output: asis
takeup = app.chose_wait_save[app.treat == 1].mean()
itt = r3.params.treat
B = app[app.treat == 1]
md_table([[("Chose it" if k else "Did not choose it"), f"{len(g):,}", f"{g.revenue_pre.mean():.2f}", f"{g.revenue_post.mean():.2f}"]
          for k, g in B.groupby("chose_wait_save")],
         ["Users in B", "N", "Revenue **before** (€)", "Revenue during (€)"], align=["l", "r", "r", "r"])
print(f"""
::: {{.incremental}}
- Only **{takeup:.0%}** of B users chose the new option.
- $\\hat\\beta_1$ = €{itt:.2f} is the effect of **being offered** the option: the **intention-to-treat (ITT)**. Still causal, and the relevant number for the launch decision.
- ❌ Don't compare choosers vs non-choosers: choosers already spent much more **before** the test → self-selection, the same problem as smokers.
- Effect on those who actually chose it ≈ ITT / take-up = {itt:.2f} / {takeup:.2f} = **€{itt / takeup:.2f}** (more on this with IV, TA8).
:::
""")
```
:::

---

## When SUTVA fails, change the unit of randomization

::: {style="font-size:0.8em"}
**SUTVA:** my outcome depends only on **my own** treatment, not on other users' treatment.
:::

```{python}
#| output: asis
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
CITY6 = ["Madrid", "Barcelona", "Paris", "London", "Berlin", "Rome"]
per = 12
s = bse_anim.Steps("level", figsize=(11, 3.9), ncols=2,
                   margins=dict(left=0.01, right=0.99, top=0.88, bottom=0.02, wspace=0.06))
a1, a2 = s.ax
def draw_cities(ax, assign, title):
    ax.set_xlim(-0.5, 3 * 4.2); ax.set_ylim(-1.3, 2 * 4.2 - 0.4); ax.axis("off"); ax.set_title(title)
    pos = {}
    for c in range(6):
        cx, cy = (c % 3) * 4.2, (1 - c // 3) * 4.2
        ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((cx - 0.3, cy - 0.3), 3.6, 3.0, fill=False, ec=GRAY, lw=1.2, ls="--"))
        ax.text(cx + 1.5, cy + 2.95, CITY6[c], ha="center", fontsize=11, color="#555")
        for j in range(per):
            x, yy = cx + (j % 4) * 1.0, cy + (j // 4) * 0.95
            ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((x, yy), 0.7, 0.6, color=T_COL if assign[c][j] else C_COL, alpha=0.9))
            pos[(c, j)] = (x + 0.35, yy + 0.3)
    return pos
ind = [rng.binomial(1, 0.5, per) for _ in range(6)]
pos = draw_cities(a1, ind, "Randomize users")
a2.set_visible(False); s.snap()
for c in (0, 4):
    tr_ = [j for j in range(per) if ind[c][j]]; co_ = [j for j in range(per) if not ind[c][j]]
    for t_, c_ in list(zip(tr_, co_))[:3]:
        a1.annotate("", xy=pos[(c, c_)], xytext=pos[(c, t_)], arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color=PURPLE, lw=1.6))
a1.text(6.0, -1.0, "B users take the shared drivers → A users wait longer", color=PURPLE, fontsize=12, ha="center")
s.snap()
a2.set_visible(True)
draw_cities(a2, [np.full(per, c in (0, 2, 4)) for c in range(6)], "Randomize cities")
a2.text(6.0, -1.0, "spillovers stay inside one arm", color=PURPLE, fontsize=12, ha="center")
s.snap()
s.show(height=330)
```

::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%" .fs72}
::: {.fragment}
**How the spillover happens.** Users in the same city share the **same pool of drivers**.
B users request extra (cheap) rides → fewer free drivers → **A users** wait longer, see surge prices, or give up → A's revenue falls **because of B**.
So $\bar Y_0$ no longer estimates $E[Y(0)]$, and $\bar Y_1 - \bar Y_0$ **overstates** the effect of launching the option for everyone.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="50%" .fs72}
::: {.fragment}
**Fix:** randomize at the level where the interaction happens: the **city** (the driver market). All users in a city see the same app, so spillovers stay *within* one arm; **cluster SEs by city**.
Cost: few units (cities) → much less power. In practice firms use many cities, or **switchback** designs (randomize city × time slot).
:::
:::
:::
